_what: The mAP yolo11n scores on the pinned COCO val2017 500-image subset, and every input that determines it. Read tests/integration/test_map_regression.py for how it is measured and src/yowo/benchmark/_baseline.py for how it is enforced.
_band: Two-sided. Repeat runs on one machine are bit-identical, so for a fixed model, fixed weights, a fixed image set AND fixed detection bounds the number should not move at all. The tolerance absorbs cross-machine float drift and nothing else. A rise past it means something changed that nobody declared.
_provenance: RE-RECORDED 2026-09-16 because this run's inputs changed: max_nms=1000 and max_det=300 now ship as defaults, and a detection bound is an input that determines the number. Measured on darwin/arm64: 38628 detections (was 44553 unbounded), mAP_50_95 0.415729 (delta -0.000047), mAP_50 0.584895 (-0.000111), mAP_75 0.450922 (-0.000004). Every delta is ~100x inside the +/-0.005 band, so the gate would have PASSED without a re-record -- it was re-recorded anyway, because the band exists to absorb float drift and not to hide a declared change. CAVEAT, named rather than buried: the previous record's cross-machine drift was measured at zero on ubuntu/x86-64 (CI run 34974724304, 2026-09-15) for the UNBOUNDED configuration. These bounded numbers have NOT yet been measured on ubuntu. MEASURED on ubuntu/x86-64 2026-09-16 (CI run 35066239948): 38628 detections -- IDENTICAL to darwin -- mAP_50_95 0.4157293959905467, mAP_50 0.5848955018590482, mAP_75 0.4509217301224101. All three agree to six decimals; mAP_75 is bit-identical and the other two differ at the 8th decimal, which is pycocotools' accumulation order and not the bound. The identical DETECTION COUNT is the load-bearing part: the pre-cap selected exactly the same candidates on both architectures, which is what the explicit index tie-break exists to guarantee. The +/-0.005 band remains headroom against a future runner image or torch bump.
_shipped_default_cost: CONTEXT, NOT ENFORCED. The engine's default confidence_threshold is 0.25, not the COCO protocol's 0.001 this baseline uses. Measured once, 2026-09-15, over the same 500 images: 0.3658, 5.0 points lower. Recorded so the gap between the published-comparable number and what a user gets out of the box is visible rather than discovered. Nothing re-measures it, so treat it as dated. The 2026-09-16 bounds do not bind there: the maximum candidate count observed at conf 0.25 over 300 real COCO images was 247, against max_nms=1000, and the maximum box count was 28, against max_det=300.
_rerecord: All three of map_50_95, map_50 and map_75 are enforced against the band. To re-record deliberately: run `pytest tests/integration/test_map_regression.py -s`, which prints all three at full precision on a `to re-record:` line, and update them together with measured_on and measured_at. A partial re-record fails the gate rather than leaving numbers that were never measured together. max_nms and max_det are required fields for the same reason every other input is: a bound changes the number, and a gate that does not record it compares across a difference it no longer knows about. The gate never writes this file; only a human in a reviewed commit does.
